Hum Toxicol 1987; 6: 331. Interactions For interactions associated with opioid analgesics, see p.103. Plasma concentrations of meptazinol may be increased by ritonavir and use together should be avoided (see also p.103). Pharmacokinetics After oral doses of meptazinol peak plasma concentra- tions have been achieved within 0.5 to 2 hours, but bio- availability is low since it undergoes extensive first- pass metabolism. Systemic availability is improved af- ter rectal doses. Peak plasma concentrations have been achieved 30 minutes after rectal or intramuscular use. Plasma protein binding has averaged only about 27%. Elimination half-lives of about 2 hours have been re- ported. Meptazinol is extensively metabolised in the liver and is excreted mainly in the urine as the glucuro- nide conjugate.
